name: Fear of Man

counsel.text: The fear of God destroys the fear of man. The three children feared God, therefore they feared not the king's wrath. Dan 3: 16. The greater noise drowns the less; the noise of thunder drowns the noise of a river; so, when the fear of God is supreme in the soul, it drowns all other carnal fear.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the first commandment

counsel.text: It is better that God approve, than man applaud. The world may put us in their rubric and God put us in his black book. What is a man the better that his fellow-prisoners commend him, if his judge condemn him?
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 10

counsel.text: In particular, a man begins to be in repute for piety, wisdom, learning, or the like,--he is spoken of much to that purpose; his heart is tickled to hear of it, and his pride and ambition affected with it. If this man now, with all his strength, ply the things from whence his repute, and esteem, and glory amongst men do spring, with a secret eye to have it increased, he is entering into temptation; which, if he take not heed, will quickly render him a slave of lust.
counsel.author: John Owen

counsel.text: Some are naturally gentle, facile, easy to be entreated, pliable; which, though it be the noblest temper of nature, and the best and choicest ground, when well broken up and fallowed for grace to grow in, yet, if not watched over, will be a means of innumerable surprisals and entanglements in temptation.
counsel.author: John Owen

counsel.text: If Christ appears for us in heaven, then we must appear for him upon earth. Christ is not ashamed to carry our names on his breast, and shall we be ashamed of his truth? Does he plead our cause, and shall we not stand up in his cause?
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's priestly office

counsel.text: It should be a Christian's ambition to wear his Saviour's livery, though it be sprinkled with blood and sullied with disgrace.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 10

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Father, I feared people more than I feared you. I kept quiet when I should have spoken, or I bent the truth to be liked, and so I was ashamed of your Son before others. I confess it honestly. Thank you that the Lord Jesus prayed for Peter before he fell and received him again afterward. He is my advocate too, and his blood was shed for this sin. Forgive me and cleanse me, as you have promised. Holy Spirit, put this fear of man to death in me, and give me a holy fear of you that is greater than every other fear. Amen.

prayers.title: When I fear what they will think
prayers.text: Lord, I am afraid of what they will think of me. Right now I want to be liked more than I want to be faithful. Help me. Remind me that you see me, that you are my judge, and that in Christ your favor is already mine. Give me courage to speak the truth in love and to own your name, whatever it costs me here. Holy Spirit, make me bold and gentle at once. Amen.

prayers.title: Not ashamed of Christ
prayers.text: Lord Jesus, you were not ashamed to call me your own. You bore scorn and shame on the cross for me. Do not let me be ashamed of you now. Steady my heart before these people. Let me care more for your approval than for their praise or their frown. Give me plain words, a quiet spirit, and the courage to do what is right in front of them. Amen.

examinationQuestions: Whose approval did you most want today, and where did that desire lead you to say, or leave unsaid, what you should not have?
When you held back from owning Christ or speaking the truth, what were you afraid of losing, and why did it seem weightier than his favor?
Did you agree to anything today only to avoid someone's displeasure? What would faithfulness have looked like instead?
Do you change your words and manner to fit the room? What would change if God's verdict on you in Christ were enough?
Who has the power to unsettle you with a look or a word? Bring that person before God and ask where they have taken his place in your heart.
Is there a truth you need to speak, a wrong you need to confess, or a refusal you need to give, that you have put off out of fear?
fleeActions: Do the faithful thing you have been putting off for fear of someone: make the call, speak the truth kindly, or say no.
Before you walk into the room you dread, stop and pray that the fear of God would be greater in you than the fear of anyone there.
Open your Bible to Isaiah 51:12-13, read it, and then say aloud before God whom you have been fearing.
If you were silent about Christ when you should have spoken, go back to that person if you can, and tell them plainly and kindly that you belong to him.
Put your phone down and stop checking for replies and reactions. Go and do the work God has given you for this hour.
Tell a trusted believer in your church what you are afraid of, and ask them to pray that you would be faithful and bold.

afterFallReadings.text: Little did Peter think he should deny and forswear his Master so soon as ever he was questioned whether he knew him or no. It was no better when the hour of temptation came; all resolutions were forgotten, all love to Christ buried; the present temptation closing with his carnal fear carried all before it.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen

afterFallReadings.text: Yea, let me add, that never any soul did or shall perish by the power of any lust, sin, or corruption, who could raise his soul by faith to an expectation of relief from Jesus Christ.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14
